title: Sharp Second Constants in $L^1$ Landau--Kolmogorov Inequalities on a Finite Interval
abstract: For every integer $n \ge 1$ and every compact interval $[a,b]$ of length $L = b - a > 0$, we determine the lexicographically sharp pair of constants in the additive all-$L^1$ Landau--Kolmogorov inequality $\|f^{(n)}\|_{L^1([a,b])} \le 4^n n! L^{-n} \|f\|_{L^1([a,b])} + \frac{L}{2} B_n \|f^{(n+1)}\|_{L^1([a,b])}$ on $W^{n+1,1}([a,b])$, establishing the exact closed-form second constant $B_n = 1 - \frac{2^n}{n+1} + \frac{2^{n+1}}{n+1}\sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor(n+1)/2\rfloor} (-1)^{k-1}\cos^{n+1}\frac{k\pi}{n+2}$. For $n = 1$ on $[0,1]$, this improves Burenkov's $1/2$ to the sharp $1/4$, resolving to the best of our knowledge the $L^1$ case of an open problem posed by Burenkov (1980). On $[-1,1]$, we construct an $(n+1)$-point moving-node divided-difference operator $T_n$ driven by the eigenvalues of a symmetric tridiagonal Jacobi matrix $J_n(x)$, disintegrating Burenkov's rank-one functional while preserving $\|T_n\|_{L^1\to L^1} = A_n := 2^n n!$, and prove unconditionally for all $n \ge 1$ that the Peano error profile $E_n$ is strictly decreasing on $[0,1]$ with unique global maximum at $t = 0$. Consequences include exact characterization of $C^{n+1}([a,b])$ extremizers (scalar multiples of rescaled $U_n$), the exact center identity $B_n = 1 - A_n E_n(W_1^{n+1})_1$ with Boyanov--Kofanov polynomial $L^1$-approximation, solution of Stechkin's optimal operator problem at minimal admissible norm $N = A_n$, strict monotonicity $\frac{1}{2} = B_1 < B_2 < \dots < 1$, and a complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the main theorem.

provenance: The project began on 2026-11-20 when Lijails and GPT 6.2 Astra (with writing assistance from Qwen 3.8 Flash) investigated the sharp second-order L^1 inequality on [0,1]. Between 2026-11-25 and 2026-11-26, Lijails collaborated with GPT 6.2 Sol to generalize the moving-node divided-difference construction and Jacobi/Gauss connections to all n >= 1 (v0.1 and v0.2 with threshold n >= 20), and with Gemini 4 Neon to discover the vertical-chord contour estimate cutting the analytic threshold to n >= 4 (leaving n = 1, 2 elementary and n = 3 certified on five subintervals). Subsequently, a multi-agent workflow coordinated by Gemini 4 Hydrogen (including GPT- and Gemini-family swarm workers plus earlier helper trials with Qwen 3.8 Flash, GPT 6 Luna Low, GPT 6.1 Terra XHigh, and CodeBuddy) produced a complete unconditional Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of Theorem 1 using zero sorry and only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], executed a primary-source literature audit uncovering Burenkov (1980, 1986) and Kofanov (1984), added the Stechkin corollary (Corollary 2) and contour-integral strict monotonicity B_{n+1} > B_n (Corollary 3), and drafted paper_hexagon.tex under Lijails's supervision.
